name: bch-cloak-apnt
description: APNT: a private note-transfer construction for Bitcoin Cash. Protocol sources, canonical proof artifacts and independent checkers.
comment: OWNERSHIP NOTE (2026-08-13): this file is normally facilitator-owned, like
the rest of public-tree/. It was edited by the build-gate task because the
gate cannot exist without real dependency declarations -- the tree declared
ZERO dependencies before this change, which is exactly why several
verifiers were miscounted as unrunnable and why `pnpm install
--frozen-lockfile` had nothing to freeze against. Facilitator should review
this file specifically.
The four verify:* scripts are ALL FOUR standalone verifiers configured in
allowlist.json's standaloneVerifiers[] (see export-manifest.json ->
standaloneVerifiers). All four were already executing during export;
README.md's 'Verify it yourself' section originally documented only the
first two -- fixed in the same pass that added the other two scripts
here, so the two files agree again.
devDependencies are the true, measured dependency set: TypeScript compiles
packages/chain-io (a real pnpm workspace member) and typechecks
packages/protocol-runtime/src (NOT a workspace member -- it ships
tsconfig.json but deliberately no package.json, so `pnpm -r` never reaches
it; scripts/public-export/build-gate.mjs typechecks it directly against
that tsconfig instead). vitest backs chain-io's declared `test` script --
disclosed here because it is easy to miss: as of this writing the
allowlist stages chain-io's package.json/tsconfig.json/2 src files but
NOT packages/chain-io/test/, so `pnpm -r test` currently matches ZERO
test files every run. That is not silently accepted: build-gate.mjs
counts vitest's own reported test-file total and REFUSES the export when
it is exactly zero (see export-manifest.json -> generation.buildGate ->
steps[] -> the 'test' step's testFilesRun field, and that file's module
header, constraint 5, for the full reasoning). A passing release's
manifest therefore always has testFilesRun > 0; a manifest recording
testFilesRun: 0 never came from a successful export.
@types/node matches the version chain-io's own package.json already pins.
Every staged SOURCE file (protocol-runtime, chain-io, the three configured
*.mjs verifiers) imports ONLY Node builtins -- scripts/public-export's own
standalone-verify.mjs measures externalDependencies==[] against a real
staged export as of this commit. These devDependencies exist to RUN the
toolchain (tsc, vitest), not because staged source needs a runtime
package. NOT wired in here: one candidate verifier that was reviewed but
is not currently allowlisted --
packages/reference-aggregator/tools/verify-apnt-import-created-note-v4-groth16-proof-independently-v0.mjs
-- whose only non-builtin import is '@noble/curves/bn254.js'. It would
need exactly one more devDependency ('@noble/curves', already pinned at
^1.9.7 in the private root lockfile) if it is allowlisted.
CORRECTION 2026-08-13: an earlier version of this comment also named
verify-apnt-live-settlement-groth16-terminal-v0.mjs as importing only
'@noble/curves/bn254.js'. That was FALSE and was measured to be false:
its only non-builtin import is '../dist/index.js' -- the compiled package
it is testing -- and it does not import @noble/curves at all. It is not a
standalone verifier and must not be counted as one. The claim was written
from a summary rather than from the file's imports.
pnpm-lock.yaml IS committed here. scripts/public-export/build-gate.mjs
generates it fresh, inside the staged tree, at gate time, then copies
that one file back into the real staged tree so it ships -- see that
file's header for why, and for what happens when the machine running the
gate is offline. It is the one build-gate-generated artifact that
survives export; everything else the toolchain produces (node_modules,
dist) dies with the isolated copy it was built in. export-manifest.json
records it at generation.buildGate.generatedLockfile (path, sha256,
size) precisely because it is generated rather than authored, unlike
every other file this comment describes.
The private repository's root package.json carries build and probe
scripts that would be dead here, so this file is written for the public
tree rather than copied into it.
All five verify:* scripts need only a bare node and nothing else: no
install, no network, no build. The export pipeline runs them inside a
filesystem-sandboxed copy of this tree (standalone-verify.mjs) before the
tree is allowed to ship; the build gate additionally runs `npm run
verify` for real, through pnpm, in the toolchain-installed staged copy --
a second, differently-shaped execution of the same claim.
`capabilities` (added later) prints capabilities.json human-readably;
`npm run capabilities -- --json` emits the raw file. capabilities.json
itself is GENERATED by scripts/public-export/generate-capabilities.mjs
(private-repo-side tooling, not shipped here) by actually running every
command above and harvesting each one's own establishes/doesNotEstablish
-- see that generator's header and capabilities.json's own `description`
and `howToUse` fields for the full contract. capabilities.mjs, by
contrast, IS shipped here: it is a tiny, dependency-free reader, not the
generator.
